title: South Korea's National Tax Service to Notify 260,000 Households That Missed Earned Income and Child Tax Credit Applications; Only 95% to Be Paid Through Dec. 1 - BigGo Finance
text:

 Add preferred source South Korea's National Tax Service will send late-application notices to 260,000 households that have not yet applied for the 2025 Earned Income Tax Credit and Child Tax Credit. The application deadline is Dec. 1, and because these households missed the regular application window, they will receive only 95% of the calculated amount. Starting this year, 10,000 additional households identified after May through newly confirmed income data are also included in the notification pool. The Earned Income Tax Credit requires meeting income thresholds by household type and holding assets below 240 million won (approximately $180,000); applications will be reviewed and paid by Jan. 15 next year. The government plans to expand the program for the 2026 tax year by raising payment caps and easing income requirements. Key Elements 
 National Tax Service Earned Income Tax Credit Child Tax Credit Hometax late application tax law amendment bill South Korea's National Tax Service is sending late-application notices to 260,000 households that have not yet applied for the 2025 Earned Income Tax Credit and Child Tax Credit. Households that receive the notice can apply through Dec. 1, but unlike those who filed during the regular May application window, they will receive only 95% of the calculated amount. Once the deadline passes, the path to receiving the credit closes entirely.
 The National Tax Service announced the late-application plan on the 2nd. Applications received will be paid on Jan. 15 next year after income and asset reviews. Starting this year, the notification pool has widened. An additional 10,000 households confirmed as potentially eligible after analyzing newly collected income data following the May regular-application notices are also included among notice recipients.
 The payment rate is divided into three tiers depending on when the application is filed. Those who applied during the regular application period from May 1 to June 1 receive the full calculated amount. From June 2 to Dec. 1, a 5% reduction applies, leaving 95%. After Dec. 2, applications are no longer possible.
 Category Application Period Payment Rate 
 Regular application May 1–June 1 100% 
 Late application June 2–Dec. 1 95% 
 No application accepted After Dec. 2 0% 
 Eligibility requirements for each credit are divided along two axes: income and assets. For the Earned Income Tax Credit, combined household income in 2025 must be below 22 million won (approximately $16,000) for single-person households, 32 million won (approximately $24,000) for single-earner households, and 44 million won (approximately $33,000) for dual-earner households. The Child Tax Credit applies to households with children under 18 whose combined income is below 70 million won (approximately $52,000). Both credits require total household assets below 240 million won (approximately $180,000), with debts not deducted. If assets are between 170 million won (approximately $130,000) and 240 million won, only half of the calculated amount is paid.
 Payment amounts range from a minimum of 30,000 won (approximately $22) to 1.65 million won (approximately $1,200) for single-person households, 2.85 million won (approximately $2,100) for single-earner households, and 3.3 million won (approximately $2,500) for dual-earner households under the Earned Income Tax Credit. The Child Tax Credit ranges from a minimum of 500,000 won (approximately $370) to a maximum of 1 million won (approximately $740) per dependent child. Even if a household applies after receiving a notice, the payment amount may differ from the estimated amount shown in the notice or payment may not be made at all, depending on the results of the full household review including financial assets.
 Application channels differ by type of notice. For postal notices, recipients can scan the QR code; for mobile notices, they can file via the "Apply" button. The automated response service (1544-9944) also operates 24 hours a day. Even households that did not receive a notice but believe they meet the income and asset requirements can apply directly through Hometax by entering information manually, attaching supporting documents such as an income confirmation certificate issued by their employer. However, in such cases, applications through the automated response service are not permitted. Whether a household is a notification target can be checked through the "Check Notification Target Status" menu on Hometax.
 The National Tax Service cited late submission of income data by employers as the reason some households did not receive notices in May. The legal deadline for submitting income data is March 10, and if submitted after that date, the income is not reflected at the time of the May regular-application notices, according to the explanation. Starting this year, the policy is to re-analyze even belatedly submitted data and supplement it through late-application notices.
 Young people with temporary income from part-time or day labor, or those currently retired but with wage, business, or clergy income in 2025, may also be eligible. Senior citizens who have difficulty using mobile devices or PCs can receive guidance on the application process at the credit counseling center (1566-3636). The counseling center operates from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. on weekdays.
 The government plans to expand the Earned Income Tax Credit program starting with the 2026 tax year to reflect minimum wage increases and inflation. According to this year's tax law amendment bill, the maximum Earned Income Tax Credit payment will rise to 1.8 million won (approximately $1,300) for single-person households, 3.1 million won (approximately $2,300) for single-earner households, and 3.6 million won (approximately $2,700) for dual-earner households. Income requirements will also be eased to below 26 million won (approximately $19,000) for single-person households, 37 million won (approximately $28,000) for single-earner households, and 52 million won (approximately $39,000) for dual-earner households. The National Tax Service said it will provide detailed guidance to potentially eligible households in line with the program expansion and reduce missed support through publicity tailored to the characteristics of each group, including young people.
